name: André Rodrigues - Proposition de la Commission
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulation (EU) 2021/2115 as regards the conditionality system, types of intervention in the form of direct payment, types of intervention in certain sectors and rural development and annual performance reports and Regulation (EU) 2021/2116 as regards data and interoperability governance, suspensions of payments annual performance clearance and controls and penalties
part_text:
The European Parliament wants to change the European Union's farming subsidy rules. It proposes exempting small farms from some environmental and animal welfare conditions attached to payments. It also wants to make it easier for farmers to get crisis payments after natural disasters, bad weather or disease outbreaks. Member States would get more flexibility to adjust their national farm plans, and the Commission would have to report on how crisis money is used.

- Small farms under 10 hectares would be exempt from many environmental conditions attached to subsidies.
- Farmers hit by disasters or animal disease outbreaks could get crisis payments more easily.
- The Parliament has set its position; talks with Member States come next before any law is final.
